# About Us

At Resonon, we understand that pushing the boundaries of research and managing production isn't
easy. When you need next-level imaging, the limits of traditional vision systems can limit
advances.

Our hyperspectral imaging cameras break through these limitations, revealing details invisible to
standard sensors and the naked eye.

By unlocking hidden information, our technology empowers researchers, scientists, engineers, and
manufacturers to solve complex problems and accelerate progress. We don't just provide equipment—we
collaborate with you to evaluate solutions and integrate technology that meets your specific
challenges so that you can start gaining new insights.

> Technical Excellence. Superior Results.

[Resonon Hyperspectral Image Processing Software optical lab]

## What Our Clients Say

**By combining our AI model with Resonon's hyperspectral imaging system, we can distinguish plastic
objects to recognize and classify waste. ** We are able to detect objects that we were once unable
to when using just RGB cameras. I am very satisfied with the purchase of the Resonon camera.
Resonon's cameras have **high spectral resolution**, making it easy to find features during
classification. They also have **high spatial resolution**, making micro-scale measurements
possible. Hyperspectral data is useful because it **provides solutions to difficult and complex
problems**.
As a university scientist,** I have been working with Resonon and using Resonon cameras for more
than 20 years.** In 2019, when I founded Spectral Analytix, it was without hesitation that I
purchased a [**Pika L**][64] as our imaging work horse.
**Based on quality and robustness of both hardware and software, I strongly recommend Resonon** as
your imaging partner. Additionally, Resonon provides unsurpassed service!

## Why Choose Resonon

A Trusted Partner
* 20+ years of hyperspectral imaging expertise with over 1000 deployed systems.
* Trusted provider to leading research entities, including [NASA][69], [NOAA][70], and [NIST][71].

Rapid Support by Hyperspectral Experts
* The hyperspectral imaging experts in our Sales Team will help you to get the right system for your
application.
* Free sample scanning answers “Will hyperspectral imaging work?” before you purchase.
* 13-day average lead time for standard systems.
* Rapid support response time, usually within one business day, at no cost—some competitors charge
for a support package to guarantee a response within 1 to 3 days.

Outstanding Hyperspectral Systems
* Resonon’s imagers provide excellent [images][72] and spectral data.
* Seamless hardware and software integration through in-house development.
* Built to last. Designed, fabricated, and assembled in the USA with a standard 2-year
warranty—systems routinely operate in the field for 10+ years.
* Exceptional Hyperspectral Software
High-quality data is not enough; Resonon software enables the conversion of ***data ***into
***useful information***.
No 3rd-party software is required to operate our systems, simplifying data processing.
* **Spectronon™**: Rated among the best hyperspectral software packages by academic and research
users—unlike our competitor’s software, you can [download Spectronon][73] and sample data for free
right now.
* **Airborne software**: We know that airborne hyperspectral can be difficult. To make it easier,
our airborne software and Spectronon handle all acquisition, geocorrection, reflectance/radiance
conversion, post-processing, and creation of clear visualizations.
* **RVS (Real-time Vision System)**: Powerful but easy-to-implement software streamlined for use in
high-throughput lab scanning and industrial applications.

## Careers

Resonon designs, manufactures, and deploys hardware and software for hyperspectral imaging in
laboratory, industrial, and airborne environments. As a small business, we offer an exciting,
friendly work environment with a flexible schedule. Our current projects span a wide range of
applications, from developing a sensor for a NASA satellite, to implementing custom machine vision
solutions for manufacturing challenges, to assisting researchers in deploying our sensors on drones.
We prioritize a healthy work-life balance.

Application Example: Hyperspectral Imaging at Night Boosts Plant Stress Detection

A Pika L hyperspectral imager was used with a halogen light to image plants inside a dark room at noon and midnight over several days.

Nighttime imaging significantly improved detection of spider mite infestations, increasing classification accuracy by 29-31%.

Published in: C. Nansen et al,. Plant Methods (2024)

# About Us

At Resonon, we understand that pushing the boundaries of research and managing production isn't
easy. When you need next-level imaging, the limits of traditional vision systems can limit
advances.

Our hyperspectral imaging cameras break through these limitations, revealing details invisible to
standard sensors and the naked eye.

By unlocking hidden information, our technology empowers researchers, scientists, engineers, and
manufacturers to solve complex problems and accelerate progress. We don't just provide equipment—we
collaborate with you to evaluate solutions and integrate technology that meets your specific
challenges so that you can start gaining new insights.

> Technical Excellence. Superior Results.

[Resonon Hyperspectral Image Processing Software optical lab]

## Why Choose Resonon

A Trusted Partner
* 20+ years of hyperspectral imaging expertise with over 1000 deployed systems.
* Trusted provider to leading research entities, including [NASA][69], [NOAA][70], and [NIST][71].

Rapid Support by Hyperspectral Experts
* The hyperspectral imaging experts in our Sales Team will help you to get the right system for your
application.
* Free sample scanning answers “Will hyperspectral imaging work?” before you purchase.
* 13-day average lead time for standard systems.
* Rapid support response time, usually within one business day, at no cost—some competitors charge
for a support package to guarantee a response within 1 to 3 days.

Outstanding Hyperspectral Systems
* Resonon’s imagers provide excellent [images][72] and spectral data.
* Seamless hardware and software integration through in-house development.
* Built to last. Designed, fabricated, and assembled in the USA with a standard 2-year
warranty—systems routinely operate in the field for 10+ years.
* Exceptional Hyperspectral Software
High-quality data is not enough; Resonon software enables the conversion of ***data ***into
***useful information***.
No 3rd-party software is required to operate our systems, simplifying data processing.
* **Spectronon™**: Rated among the best hyperspectral software packages by academic and research
users—unlike our competitor’s software, you can [download Spectronon][73] and sample data for free
right now.
* **Airborne software**: We know that airborne hyperspectral can be difficult. To make it easier,
our airborne software and Spectronon handle all acquisition, geocorrection, reflectance/radiance
conversion, post-processing, and creation of clear visualizations.
* **RVS (Real-time Vision System)**: Powerful but easy-to-implement software streamlined for use in
high-throughput lab scanning and industrial applications.

## Careers

Resonon designs, manufactures, and deploys hardware and software for hyperspectral imaging in
laboratory, industrial, and airborne environments. As a small business, we offer an exciting,
friendly work environment with a flexible schedule. Our current projects span a wide range of
applications, from developing a sensor for a NASA satellite, to implementing custom machine vision
solutions for manufacturing challenges, to assisting researchers in deploying our sensors on drones.
We prioritize a healthy work-life balance.

Bozeman, Montana is our home base. This lively university town offers excellent schools and is just
minutes away from world-class skiing, mountain biking, fishing, white-water boating, and rock
climbing.

**We do not currently have any open positions.**

## #1 Optical Manufacturer Advantages

Our ability to provide high precision optics at the best price/performance ratios makes us the
perfect partner.

S.O. has over 60 years of optical design, optimization and manufacturing experience with a presence
in North America

All design and manufacturing are done in-house, so we have full control of each stage starting with
the raw materials to the finished products.

## Global Custom Optics Manufacturing Facility and Capabilities

Shanghai Optics design, manufacture and assemble custom lens systems/optical components from our
global manufacturing facility. Learn about our capabilities, which includes diamond turning aspheric
lens manufacturing, high laser damage threshold optical coating and state of the art metrology.

## Custom Optical Engineering Solutions

[Lens System Design]

#### Lens System Design

No matter what kind of custom optical design you're looking for, our custom lens manufacturer will
make your vision a reality. We provide custom objectives including deep ultraviolet applications to
infrared photography, metrology, monitoring, microscopy and other custom optical lenses. Our
projection lens designers and concept evaluation teams are the best at what they do.

[Tools and Softwares]

#### Tools and Softwares

Part of our custom optical engineering solutions includes the utilization of the latest and most
innovative technologies. Our team of experienced engineers use Zemax®, CODE V® and ASAP® for
simulation and modeling techniques. Our network of mechanical engineers use SolidWorks® and
Pro/ENGINEER® for custom optical design and complex COSMOS® to conduct thermal analysis and other
simulations like diffraction light and stray light analysis.

[Illumination System Design]

#### Illumination System Design

We're proud to be a custom lens manufacturer that specializes in designing automated lighting
systems, street lights and other indoors and outdoor lighting design systems. We also provide custom
components, individual design and customized services to meet and exceed your expectations.

With a robust portfolio that includes lab and portable reflectometers, emissometers, and hyperspectral cameras, the company serves diverse markets such as aerospace, defense, solar energy, and materials science, providing innovative solutions for research and quality control. Trusted for over 50 years, Surface Optics Corporation is dedicated to delivering precise and reliable measurement tools to meet the evolving needs of its customers.

Trusted for 50 Years in Optical Properties Characterization

Surface Optics offers a single engineering and manufacturing source for solutions requiring the application, characterization, or control of the optical properties of surfaces.

Founded in 1977 to provide optical property measurement services, today Surface Optics Corporation (SOC) specializes in advanced imaging systems, scientific instruments and thin film vacuum coatings for surface engineering.

SOC is pioneering innovative solutions for our research, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, automotive, and energy customers worldwide.

Products

Hyperspectral and Multispectral Imaging Systems

development applications, the SOC410 Series Reflectometers produce precision measurements with
excellent agreement to complex benchtop instrumentation in an easy-to-use handheld package. A
touchscreen interface provides guided calibration, sample identification, and measurement data
display.

**Can I rent a 410 Series Reflectometer? Do you provide measurement services?**

Yes, we rent to customers in the United States and internationally in countries with a Surface
Optics distributor. Our measurements lab provides reflectance and emittance measurement services,
including SRI and TSR reporting.

**Do I need to make contact with the sample to perform a measurement?**

The SOC410 Series reflectometers are designed to be used as a contact measurement device. The
integrating sphere port is pressed directly against the surface being measured. Customers looking
for a non-contact measurement may still acquire useful data but should expect decreased accuracy
from the provided specifications. Contact our team for more information on how this will affect
system performance.

**What is the minimum sample size / sampling port size?**

The sample port is 1.32 cm (0.52 inches) and should be completely covered for the best performance
from the system.

******What is the difference between the 410-Solar and 410-Solar-i?******

There are two 410-Solar models, the 410-Solar provides total, specular and diffuse reflectance. The
410-Solar-i has a larger beam size which increases accuracy for non-uniform surfaces. It has a lower
price point, faster measurements, and only requires calibration with one coupon but is limited to
providing total solar reflectance without breaking down the specular and diffuse percentage.

********What is the maximum temperature a sample can be without damaging the reflectometer?********

The samples should not exceed 100 C. The ET100 can calculate high temperature emittance from room
temperature measurements.

**********Which 410 model takes **********Total Solar reflectance (TSR) / Solar Reflectance (SR) /
Solar Reflectance Index (SRI)********** measurements?**********

The 410-Solar-I measures solar reflectance, also called total solar reflectance (TSR). The ET100
measures thermal emittance, both solar reflectance and thermal emittance are necessary to calculate
the SRI of a material. The 410-VIS-IR package includes the 410-Solar-i measurement head, the ET100
measurement head, and a single command module that operates both measurement heads. The 410-VIS-IR
will measure SRI.

************What Is the accuracy and noise floor of the 410 Series measurement, i.e. minimum
measurable reflectance? ************

The reflectance accuracy to ± 0.02-0.03 reflectance units depending on the model. The noise floor
varies depending on the sample material. If you are measuring a specular surface, like a mirror,
then the standard deviation between measurements will be extremely low, on the order of 0.001
reflectance units (where 1.0 is 100% reflective). For a diffuse sample, like a matte paint, the
standard deviation might be closer to 0.005.

**************What is the difference in the emissivity measurements provided by the 410-DHR, ET10
and ET100?**************

All three models measure directional hemispherical reflectance (DHR). The 410-DHR and ET10 provide
in-band emittance for their spectral bands (calculation of one minus reflectance, or E = 1 – DHR).
The ET100 uses the DHR to provide directional emittance at 20 degrees, directional emittance at 60
degrees, and total hemispherical emittance.

****************Can the 410 reflectometers measure curved surfaces?****************

The 410 Series reflectometers can readily collect the reflectance of samples with a radius of
curvature of 6 inches for convex surfaces and 12 inches for concave surfaces. Beyond that, you will
observe increasing uncertainty in the measurement. If you have materials that are more curved than
the provided specifications, the best way to understand the system is to fabricate a few control
samples that only differ in the sample geometry (i.e. flat and curved samples) to see if they yield
the same reflectance values, and develop a calibration/correction curve if necessary.

******************What is the difference between NIST and Non-NIST Calibration
Coupons?******************

The NIST traceable coupon is an optional upgrade. NIST traceable coupons are individually measured
against a NIST standard. For the Non-NIST coupons, we use several candidates from each manufacturing
run and measure these to produce a batch average, which we use for all coupons in that manufacturing
run.

# SOC-410 DHR Reflectometer

## Infrared reflectance measurements

The 410-DHR is a product of collaboration between U.S. Naval Air Systems Command and Surface Optics,
with vital input from the Naval Research Lab (NRL) and National Institute of Standards and
Technology (NIST). It was developed to answer a broad need for a portable device for the
verification of the optical properties of large objects in the field. The 410-DHR measures the
integrated surface reflectance of a surface at two angles of incidence (20° and 60°) and for six
wavelength bands in the .9 to 12 μm spectral range.

# 410-VIS-IR Reflectometer

## Solar reflectance and thermal emittance measurements

The 410-Vis-IR joins the ET100 and 410-Solar measurement heads in a single package for measuring
solar reflectance/absorptance and thermal emittance. The ET100 measurement head collects directional
reflectance from 1.5 to 21 μm to determine directional and total hemispherical emissivity. The
410-Solar measures reflectance at near-normal incidence from 335-2500nm. Easily switch between
reflectance and emittance data collection with a single handle for data display and measurement
controls.

# 410-Solar Reflectometer

## Measure specular, diffuse and total solar reflectance

The 410-Solar Reflectometer conforms to ASTM E903 and C1549, the standard test methods for solar
reflectance measurements. Measures reflectance at near-normal incidence for seven spectral bands.
The 410-Solar specifies the specular and diffuse components of the total reflectance. Choose from
eight solar irradiance functions, including air mass 0, 1, 1.5, and 2.0, to calculate total solar
reflectance/absorptance.

[Datasheet][64]

### ASTM Compliant

Compliant with ASTM E903, E408,
C1549 & E1980.

### 7 discrete bands

335-380 nm, 400-540 nm, 480-600 nm, 590-720 nm, 700-1100 nm, 1000-1700 nm, 1700-2500 nm.

### Multiple solar irradiance functions

New or custom functions can be added to the default options.

### Analysis of total reflectance

Identify specular and diffuse components of total reflectance.

### Fast Calibration

One minute calibration at start of measurement session

### Immediate Data

Touch screen display for data review and management

## 410-Vis-IR Applications

410-Solar data is valuable for the following applications:

Maintenance of solar fields
Evaluation of mirrors
Cool roofing and green building
Observatory telescope mirrors
Space coatings and materials

## Touchscreen User Interface

The 410-Solar touchscreen interface provides:
* Guided calibration
* Sample labeling
* Measurement data display
* Solar irradiance function selection

**What is the difference between the 410-Solar and the 410-Solar-i?**

The 410-Solar provides total, specular and diffuse reflectance. The 410-Solar-i has a larger beam
size which increases accuracy for non-uniform surfaces. It has faster measurements, and only
requires calibration with one coupon but is limited to providing total solar reflectance without the
breakdown of specular and diffuse percentage.

**Does the 410-Solar measure solar reflectance or solar absorptance?**

Solar absorptance = 1 – solar reflectance – solar transmittance; therefore, it can yield solar
absorptance only if the test material is solar opaque. Displaying solar absorptance instead of solar
reflectance is a software option.

****How is specular and diffuse reflectance measured?****

When reading the data in an excel spreadsheet you will have reflectance data points (Total, Diffuse,
Specular) for each spectral band. Your instrument measures absolute reflectance using an internal
source and integrating sphere. During a measurement, a specular beam port opens and closes letting
out specular beam, allowing for measurement of total reflectance and diffuse (scattered) reflected
energy.

# ET-10 Emissometer

## Emittance at 3-5 and 8-12 microns

The ET-10 Emissometer answers the long-standing need for measuring emissivity as an entry parameter
for calibrating infrared thermography devices. The ET-10 measures total reflectance and directional
emissivity at 20 degrees angle of incidence for 3-5 and 8-12 microns. The 8-12 band can optionally
be extended to 14 microns. View results immediately on the touchscreen display.

**What is the difference in the emissivity measurements provided by the 410-DHR, ET10 and ET100?**

All three models measure directional hemispherical reflectance (DHR). The 410-DHR and ET10 provide
in-band emittance for thir spectral bands using the calculation of one minus reflectance, or E = 1 –
DHR. The ET100 uses the DHR to provide in-band emittance values plus a single value for directional
emittance at 20 degrees, directional emittance at 60 degrees, and total hemispherical emittance.

**Is there a way to extrapolate higher temperature emissivity from room temperature measurements?**

The basic property measured by the ET100 is reflectance. Since reflectance is a physical constant,
temperature independent, it can be used to determine an accurate emissivity value if the
interrogated surface does not undergo a physical or a chemical change between the measurement at
ambient temperature and the high temperature. The ET100 measures emissivity of an object at ambient
temperature, and the user sets in the instrument the desired higher temperature, and it will
calculate emissivity for that temperature.

**Why do I need to select if the sample is metal or dielectric?**

The metal and dielectric look up tables store values of a correlation factor for a range of
Directional Thermal Emissvity (DTE) 20°. This correlation factor defines the relationship between
DTE20° and THE and it is different for metals versus dielectrics. DTE20° is measured and multiplied
by the correct correlation factor to yield THE. DTE60° is not used in this calculation.

**How is the Total Hemispherical Emissivity (THE) calculated?**

The near normal directional emissivity values are used to derive total total hemispherical
emissivity utilizing correlations published Siegel and Howell, Thermal Radiation Heat Transfer,
Taylor and Francis, 1992. The ratio of total hemispherical emittance to near-normal directional
thermal emittance is plotted as a function of near-normal directional thermal emittance. There is a
curve for metals and a curve for dielectrics. These correlations are stored as tables in the ET100
software and used to calculate total hemispherical emittance from the measured near-normal
directional thermal emittance. While the ET100 measures directional thermal emissivity at 20 and 60
degrees angle of incidence, only the DTE20° is used to calculate the total hemispherical emissivity.

**Which test method from ASTM E408 applies to the ET100?**

Test Method C.

# 410-LIDAR Reflectometer

## Reflectance at 850nm, 905nm, 940nm and 1550nm

The 410-LIDAR measures reflectance simultaneously at four key wavelengths employed by lidar systems.
Collect measurements on materials and objects that cannot easily be brought into the lab. Fast
calibration and measurement times without sacrificing measurement accuracy and repeatability. Option
to customize wavelengths.

[DATASHEET][64]
[410-Lidar Reflectometer in handheld configuration]

### **NIR and SWIR wavebands**

## Custom Spectral Bands

SOC410 Series Reflectometers use a broadband light source with spectral band distribution achieved
by a set of optical filters in front of photodetectors. By modifying these filters and detectors, we
can design a measurement head with custom spectral bands to enhance spectral resolution for
application-specific regions of interest.

## Measurement Head Modifications

**APERTURE ADJUSTMENTS**

The standard source aperture is 12 mm but can be modified for smaller samples or target areas. The
minimum source aperture size is 2mm. Decreasing the size of the source aperture results in a smaller
beam spot size (the sample port diameter remains the same). It is important to note that reducing
the aperture size will potentially decrease signal-to-noise performance. Our team would be happy to
model potential SNR changes for your materials.

**AUTOMATED / REMOTE MEASUREMENTS**

410 Series reflectometers can be converted to a rigid optic coupling with an extended focal point
for non-contact measurements, as well as mounting assistance for RCU units to be incorporated into a
larger robotic system.

**INCIDENCE ANGLES**

410 Series reflectometers can be converted to a rigid optic coupling with an extended focal point
for non-contact measurements, as well as mounting assistance for RCU units to be incorporated into a
larger robotic system.

**SAMPLE PORT CHANGES**

Additionally, the standard polyurethane port o-ring, which protects samples during the measurement
process, can be removed or replaced with a different material to meet specific application
requirements.

## Custom Verification Coupons

We can also provide customized verification coupons to offer extra assurance for quality control and
to establish a known standard with optical properties similar to a target sample. These tailored
coupons enhance the reliability of reflectance measurements by ensuring that the handheld
reflectometers are calibrated correctly and consistently accurate.

## Software Interface

410 Series reflectometers have a robust operating software, designed to meet the needs of most users
for general operation and data review. However, we understand that certain projects require more
specialized capabilities. To address these specific operational environments, we offer custom
software development services, adding unique features and functionalities tailored to your
particular requirements, such as:
* Solar transmittance measurement mode
* Engineering/technician mode for improved data security protocols
* Remote listening mode for measurement automation

# SOC410 Accessories & Maintenance

## Calibration Coupons

Calibration coupons are reference materials made from stable and homogeneously coated materials with
precisely known reflectance properties in the spectral bands of SOC410 Series reflectometers.
Calibration coupons are necessary to ensure the accuracy of 410 Series reflectance measurements.

Please use our contact form to request a quote for new calibration coupon(s) and include the serial
number of your instrument so we can confirm the correct calibration coupons for your instrument are
provided.

**Not sure if your calibration coupons should be replaced?**

Send a sample data and log file for your instrument and our team will be happy to help assess if
there are measurement errors due to compromised calibration coupons.

**NIST Traceable Coupons**

Surface Optics offers both standard and NIST traceable calibration coupons. For standard coupons,
several candidates from each manufacturing run are measured to produce a batch average. NIST
traceable coupon(s) is an optional upgrade. NIST traceable coupons are individually measured against
a NIST standard, and a Calibration Certificate is generated for the individual coupon. Calibration
data is available for an additional fee.

## Service Plans

Getting your 410 Series Reflectometer tuned and factory calibrated is the best way to ensure that it
maintains its high level of measurement integrity throughout the instrument’s lifetime. We recommend
annual servicing and replacement of calibration coupons to keep your reflectometer operating at peak
performance.

2000 uses, at the discretion of the user.

## Next-generation hyperspectral imaging for research & industry

The 710-HyCore hyperspectral camera and 710-OmniCore hyperspectral imaging system, build on our
proven SOC-710 platform.

### ****HyCore VNIR Hyperspectral Camera****

Built around a proprietary spectrograph design and co-engineered optics and sensor, the
next-generation 710 Series delivers strong performance right out of the box. Our default 1x spectral
binning reflects this—providing the signal and resolution needed without relying on binning as a
workaround. Ideal for integrators or as a complete hyperspectral imaging system when paired with the
710 Lab Tower with translation stage.

### ****OmniCore VNIR Hyperspectral Imaging System****

The 710-OmniCore hyperspectral imaging system stands out with its internal scanning design, making
it the most versatile hyperspectral imaging system available. It can be used as a lab benchtop
system, mounted to a tripod, boom, or tower for field work, or attached to a microscope—without the
need for external scanning hardware. For labs focused on long-term value, the SOC710 provides the
performance and flexibility to grow with their research.

### ****710 Lab Tower****

Pair the 710‑HyCore or OmniCore with a 710 Lab Tower to capture consistently high‑quality
hyperspectral data from day one. The rigid tower ensures repeatable alignment and controlled
geometry, while the smooth, programmable stage maintains constant scan speed to match integration
time, frame rate, and sample motion. With stable, uniform illumination, this integrated setup
minimizes motion blur, misregistration, and radiometric striping so your algorithms can fully
capitalize on clean, reliable material signatures.

### ****HyCore VNIR Hyperspectral Camera****

Built around a proprietary spectrograph design and co-engineered optics and sensor, the
next-generation 710 Series delivers strong performance right out of the box. Our default 1x spectral
binning reflects this—providing the signal and resolution needed without relying on binning as a
workaround. Ideal for integrators or as a complete hyperspectral imaging system when paired with the
710 Lab Tower with translation stage.

### ****OmniCore VNIR Hyperspectral Imaging System****

The 710-OmniCore hyperspectral imaging system stands out with its internal scanning design, making
it the most versatile hyperspectral imaging system available. It can be used as a lab benchtop
system, mounted to a tripod, boom, or tower for field work, or attached to a microscope—without the
need for external scanning hardware. For labs focused on long-term value, the SOC710 provides the
performance and flexibility to grow with their research.

### ****710 Lab Tower****

Pair the 710‑HyCore or OmniCore with a 710 Lab Tower to capture consistently high‑quality
hyperspectral data from day one. The rigid tower ensures repeatable alignment and controlled
geometry, while the smooth, programmable stage maintains constant scan speed to match integration
time, frame rate, and sample motion. With stable, uniform illumination, this integrated setup
minimizes motion blur, misregistration, and radiometric striping so your algorithms can fully
capitalize on clean, reliable material signatures.

## Live multispectral video acquisition and processing

LightShift™ captures and processes spectral data at video rates and performs live automated
calibration and spectral correlation algorithm processing. Employing a novel plenoptic spectral
imaging design, LightShift cameras offer customizable sixteen-band filter sets to tailor
multispectral imaging detection to your application.

**HIGH PERFORMANCE MULTISPECTRAL IMAGING**

### Real Time Processing

Snapshot spectral imagers obtain the entire spectral dataset during a single detector integration
period, which provides a distinct advantage in spectral imaging of fast-changing phenomena.

The amount of information generated by snapshot systems is still a key challenge since their
application to many practical tasks depends on the ability to process substantial volumes of data to
make decisions in real time. A snapshot multispectral video system must process at rates keeping
pace with the real-time acquisition of images.

LightShift is unique in its capability to process images spectrally in real time, from initial gain
and offsets compensation to spectroradiometric calibration through decision-oriented processing,
including spectral correlation using varied algorithms.

### OEM Solutions
* VNIR, SWIR or MWIR spectral ranges
* Initial spectral data collection and reduction for modeling imaging system performance
* Modification of spectral band count to increase spatial resolution
* Filter array design and manufacturing
* Camera housing and mechanical design for environmental considerations
* Industry-specific interface of USB, GigE
* System assembly, alignment, calibration and testing
* Software GUI and spectral algorithm development

**SOFTWARE**

## LightShift Pro

The LightShift PRO Software application operates in two modes: live video imaging mode or playback
of stored video mode. The user has the option to stream live video from the camera and playback
stored video simultaneously in two separate windows within the LightShift application window. The
software also supports multiple playback windows running simultaneously.

LightShift produces accurate light field, spectral and spatial resolution by using a micro-lens
array (MLA) as a series of field lenses. Each lens distributes a point in the image scene received
through the objective lens across an area of a detector array (focal plane array), forming a
hyperspectral detector Super-pixel. Each sub-pixel within a Super-pixel receives light that has
passed through the color filter array used to spectrally characterize the object. The micro-lens
spatially corrects the focused image point and projects the same image scene point onto all
sub-pixels within a Super-pixel.

Due to the positioning of the 4×4 filter array on the lens’s front aperature, it can easily be
replaced with a new filter array so that the camera can be re-tasked for different applications
requiring different wavelengths.

# DuoChrome-SM

## Real-time, 2-band SWIR/MWIR imaging system

The DuoChrome-SM can be used locally or over a network in demanding analysis, quality control, and
detection work. Comprising a very high-speed, high-sensitivity InSb array (512 x 512 pixels),
optics, and imaging electronics, the DuoChrome-SM can acquire and process imagery at a rate of 150
frames (512 x 512 pixels) per second at 14-bit resolution. The system’s spectral response is in the
short to medium wave-infrared spectral range from 1.5-5 microns in two bands: 1.5-3.0 and 3.5-5.0
microns. The HS data cube size is 1 MB. All image processing occurs at the full cube rate. The
DuoChrome‐SM imager is supported by custom DuoChrome software with a user-friendly GUI.

# SOC-750 Midwave Infrared Hyperspectral Imager

## Real-time, military-grade, MWIR hyperspectral imaging system

Comprising a very high-speed, high-sensitivity MWIR array and imaging spectrometer, the SOC-750 is
ideal for dynamic scene applications. The SOC-750 can acquire and process spectral imagery at a rate
of 11 cubes (256 x 240 pixels x 42 bands) per second at 14-bit resolution. Lower spatial resolution
cubes can be acquired at higher speeds. Covering the 2-5 μm spectral range, the SOC-750 is offered
in two configurations, using a different focal plane and tradeoffs in spectral resolution, spatial
resolution, temporal resolution, sensitivity, and maximum viewable radiance.

[Datasheet][64]

### Real-Time

11 datacubes per second

### MWIR

2.0 to 5.0 micron region

### Expert Support

Training and support by hyperspectral product engineers

### Open Data Format

Compatible with third-party spectral analysis software

### High Resolution

Option for 512 x 512 spatial pixels and 64 spectral bands

### Microscope Attachment

Features as small as 10 μm

## Applications

Gas leak detection and monitoring
Chemical identification and quantification
Target discrimination

### High Spectral Resolution

Real-time applications such as machine vision, biological screening, and chemical leak detection
require immediate feedback. The SOC750’s unique processor performs on-the-fly hyperspectral
processing at supercomputer speeds, overcoming the processing bottleneck inherent in most
hyperspectral processing systems. With multiple matched filters examining incoming data and three
spectral integrators, the SOC750 processor supports many common processing challenges.

# SOC-760 VNIR-SWIR Hyperspectral Imager

## Custom VNIR-SWIR Hyperspectral Imaging System

The SOC-760 hyperspectral imaging system is uniquely suited for lab and ground-based applications
requiring high-resolution spectral data collection for the full visible near-infrared (Vis-NIR) to
short wavelength infrared (SWIR) range. The SOC-760 is a portable dual-band, single field-of-view
system that provides coverage from 0.4 μm to 2.5 μm and captures 650 co-registered bands into a
single data cube.

[Datasheet][64]

### VNIR to SWIR

400 – 2500 nm

### High Spectral Resolution

2.5 – 5 nm

### **Training & Support**

Install includes training by our hyperspectral experts

### Open Data Format

Compatible with third-party spectral analysis software

### Co-registered

650 bands registered images into a single data cube

### Internal Scanning

Flexible target distance

## Applications

Art analysis
Art conservation
Archeology
Agriculture
Food processing
Industrial quality control

# Services

## Optical Properties Measurements

### [Hemispherical Directional Reflectance][64]

Hemispherical directional reflectance (HDR) measures the fraction of the light incident on a sample
at a given angle that is reflected back into the hemisphere. Typical HDR measurements are made out
to 25 μm. HDR as a function of reflected polar angle, polarization, wavelength, and temperature.

[More Info][65]

### Emissivity

Emissivity measures a surface’s thermal radiation relative to an ideal black body (0 to 1 scale). An
emissivity of 0 indicates a perfect reflector, while 1 signifies a perfect emitter. Accurate
emissivity is vital for non-contact temperature measurements and heat transfer calculations,
influenced by material, surface, temperature, wavelength, and angle.

[More INFO][66]

### Scatter / BSDF

Bidirectional reflectance measurement capabilities span the range from 0.3 μm to beyond 14 μm with a
full four degrees of angular freedom (incident polar and azimuthal angle, and reflected polar and
azimuthal angle). These measurements are typically made broadband or at a series of
customer-specified wavelengths.

[MORE INFO][67]

### ASTM Testing

ASTM standards for optical property testing are developed through a collaborative process involving
industry and scientific experts. Surface Optics has actively contributed to defining these testing
methodologies, leveraging decades of experience as an optical property testing lab and
instrumentation manufacturer.

[MORE INFO][68]

### Absorptance & Emittance

Surface Optics provides precise solar absorptance (α) and thermal emittance (ε) measurements,
adhering to ASTM standards for optical property testing. With decades of expertise, we deliver
reliable data to support thermal control and material optimization across industries.

[MORE INFO][69]

### SRI / TSR

Solar reflectance measures a material’s ability to reflect solar energy, expressed as a percentage
or a value from 0 to 1, where 0 means no reflectance and 1 indicates total reflectance. Backed by
decades of expertise, our lab ensures accurate, reliable solar reflectance data to support your
project’s success.

[MORE INFO][70]

## Vacuum Deposition Coatings

### Vacuum Deposited Gold (VDG)

Our VDG coating processes have been certified by major aerospace corporations such as Northrup
Grumman, Lockheed Martin, JPL, and Raytheon. Coatings can be modified to enhance reflection,
durability, and wavelength range.

[MORE INFO][71]

### Anti-Reflection (AR)

Anti-reflection coatings are designed to minimize reflection and maximize light transmission across
specified wavelength ranges. These coatings can be tailored to improve optical performance,
durability, and environmental resistance for a variety of applications.

[More Info][72]

### Spaceflight & Thermal Control

Over 30 years of expertise in precision thermal control and reflectance coatings for critical
spaceflight hardware. From design to completion, capabilities include specialized fixturing and safe
processing of aerospace components.

[More INFO][73]

### Vacuum Deposited Aluminum (VDA)

We offer standard, enhanced, or protected aluminum coating on your substrate. Our in-house design
and measurement capabilities allow for customized VDA coatings for your substrate and application.

[MORE INFO][74]

### Low Observable / Stealth

We use optical coating expertise to create unique, spectrally tailored paints. Releasable PVD thin
film coatings are processed into spectrally tailored flake pigment. Wavelength-dependent reflectance
and absorption can be customized to customer requirements using design principles of optical
interference coatings.

[MORE INFO][75]

### Large Area

Electron beam (Ebeam) evaporation or physical vapor deposition (PVD) process to coat large area
coatings up to 2.5-3m in diameter (depending on geometry) in a batch system, or 60” wide in our Roll
to Roll system.

[MORE INFO][76]

### Roll-to-Roll

unique roll-to-roll coating process was developed in-house for Electron Beam, Jori Source and Ion
Assisted Deposition (IAD) of metallic and dielectric films (all processes scalable).

[MORE INFO][77]

### Diamond-Like Carbon

Diamond-like carbon (DLC) coatings have a broad range of industrial applications due to their
superior mechanical properties such as high hardness, low friction, and promising wear resistance.
Our DLC coatings are low absorption protective coating with little shift. Deposited using a Filtered
Cathodic Arc Instrument.

[MORE INFO][78]

### High Reflectance

Custom coatings developed per customer requirements. Multilayer design engineering and coating
ability allow SOC to create custom designs for your application. Vacuum deposition Electron Beam
technology is used to minimize weight addition to your substrate.

[MORE INFO][79]

## Custom Engineering

### Electro-Optics Engineering

Our electro-optics engineering services cover full product development – from feasibility studies
through prototyping and production. Surface Optics has over twenty years of R&D program experience,
specializing in custom industrial infrared spectroscopy and imaging spectroscopy systems.

[MORE INFO][80]

### SBIR/STTR

Awarded our first SBIR Phase I contract in 1986, since then Surface Optics has consistently turned
SBIR R&D efforts into market-ready solutions. We welcome potential STTR partners to collaborate with
us on cutting-edge research.

## BRDF, transmittance, solar absorptance and emittance testing services.

Surface Optics’ founders pioneered the design of analytical instrumentation for hemispherical and
bidirectional reflectance measurements and established Surface Optics in 1977 to meet the optical
properties testing needs of the aerospace and defense industry. Today our lab serves customers in
commercial electronics, solar energy, biomedical technology, computer-generated imagery, cool
roofing, construction, and many other applications requiring optical data for heat transfer
modeling. Surface Optics customers receive the same high-quality testing and analysis we use for our
own AS9100 coatings lab.

Our mission is to provide accurate measurements with quick turnaround times, affordable costs, and
superior customer support for our unique service offerings. We welcome both U.S. and international

## Available Testing Services

### Hemispherical Directional Reflectance

Measures the fraction of the light incident on a sample at a given angle that is reflected back into
the hemisphere. Measurements of HDR from 0.3 μm to 50 μm. Typical HDR measurements are made out to
25 μm. We measure HDR as a function of incident elevation, polarization, wavelength, temperature,
and provide both the specular and diffuse components.

[MORE INFO][65]

### Scatter, BSDF, BRDF, BTDF

The bidirectional reflectance (BRDF) and bidirectional transmittance (BTDF) of a surface are defined
as the ratios of the luminous radiance reflected or transmitted into a unit solid angle to the total
incident radiance. BRDF/BTDF measurement capabilities span from 0.4 μm to 14 μm with a full four
degrees of angular freedom (incident elevation and azimuth, and reflected elevation and azimuth).

[MORE INFO][66]

### Emissivity

From reflectance measurements (and transmittance where necessary), we generate emittance data as a
function of polarization, wavelength, angle, and temperature.

# Hemispherical Directional Reflectance

## Non-contact, non-destructive specular reflectance and transmittance characterization

Hemispherical directional reflectance (HDR) measures the fraction of the light incident on a sample
at a given angle that is reflected back into the hemisphere. Typical HDR measurements are made out
to 25 μm. We measure HDR as a function of reflected polar angle, polarization, wavelength,
temperature, and provide both the specular and diffuse components.

[GET A QUOTE][64]
Cary 5000

## Instrumentation

**Cary 5000 UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometer with a DRA 2500 attachment**
* Measure 175 to 3300 nm using a PbSmart NIR detector for extended photometric range
* Extended dynamic range by attenuating the reference beam more in line with the sample absorbance
* Maximum light throughput using Schwarzchild coupling optics for higher accuracy at low
transmission levels
* Minimal noise and stray light using a floating aluminum casting and double Littrow monochromator

SOC-100 Hemispherical Directional Reflectometer

**SOC-100 HDR**
* Parallel, perpendicular & unpolarized reflectance at 12 user-selected angles between 8° and 80°.
* Separation of the reflectance into diffuse and specular components.
* Collimated and scattered transmittance at 0° incidence.
* Directional emittance as a function of wavelength and temperature beyond 500°C.
* Total hemispherical emittance as a function of temperature.

# Emissivity Measurements

## Emittance data as a function of polarization, wavelength, angle, and temperature

Emissivity is the ratio of the thermal radiation of a surface relative to the radiation of an ideal
black body at the same temperature (ratio between 0 and 1). An emissivity of 0 means that the
material is a perfect reflector, whereas a ratio of 1 means it is a perfect emitter.

The determination of surface emissivity is important for accurate non-contact temperature
measurements and for heat transfer calculations. The emissivity of a surface depends on the material
(i.e., chemical and physical properties), the nature of the surface (e.g., smooth or rough), the
temperature, wavelength, and angle.

[GET A QUOTE][64]

## Applications

Thermal emittance data is valuable for the following applications:

Radiative heat transfer analysis
Thermal shielding
Spacecraft thermal control
Temperature measurements
Energy efficiency analysis
Infrared signature management
Aerospace component testing

## Emissivity Measurement Types
* Directional, near-normal emittance, when reflectance has been measured at near normal incidence (θ
= 10°)
* Directional angular emittance, when reflectance has been measured at any incidence angle other
than near-normal
* Total hemispherical emittance, when reflectance has been measured over a sufficiently wide range
of incidence angles to permit integration over the hemisphere.
* Spectral hemispherical emittance, when reflectance has been measured over a sufficiently wide
range of incidence angles to permit integration over the hemisphere.

# BSDF / Scatter

## Scatter, BSDF, BRDF and BTDF Measurement Services

Bidirectional reflectance measurement capabilities span the range from .4 μm to beyond 14 μm with a
full four degrees of angular freedom (incident polar and azimuthal angle, and reflected polar and
azimuthal angle). BSDF measurements fully quantify not only how much a sample reflects, but also
exactly where the reflected energy goes. These measurements are typically made broadband, or at a
series of customer specified wavelengths.

[GET A QUOTE][64]

## Applications

Aerospace & black materials
Semiconductor quality control
Photorealistic rendering
Illumination design
Roughness control
Reflector material characterization
Cosmetics
LCD backlighting
Optical sensors
SOC210 Bidirectional Reflectometer

## Instrumentation
* Detectors and bandpass filters are provided to measure the BRDF to a noise floor of <10-3 sr-1
over the spectral range 3.0 to 12.0 mm.
* Horizontal sample mounting for measurement of samples, including powders and liquids.
* Repeatability to within 5% of the noise floor, with an accuracy of ~ 10% near-normal calibrated to
a diffuse reflectance.
* Complete automation for all four goniometric coordinates (Θ and Φ, incident and reflected angles);
automatically switching between the calibration reference and the sample.
* Integrated electronics and control station for processing, display, and storage the data.

## How BRDF Works

The function used to describe the directional dependence of the reflected energy from a surface is
the Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF).

The BRDF is defined as the ratio of the reflected radiance (w-m^{-2} -sr^{-1} ) in a particular
direction (θr ,φr) to the incident irradiance (w-m ^{-2 }) from direction (θi , φi).

# Transmittance Measurements

## Non-contact, non-destructive transmittance characterization

Transmittance is a critical parameter in optical analysis, determining the amount of light that
passes through a material. Our laboratory is equipped to offer precise transmittance measurements
derived from hemispherical directional reflectance (HDR) measurements. This measurement is essential
for understanding the optical properties of materials used in various industries, including
aerospace, automotive, solar energy, and coatings.

[GET A QUOTE][64]

## Understanding Hemispherical Directional Transmittance (HDT)

The hemispherical directional transmittance (HDT) represents the ratio of the total transmitted
power to the total incident power. It is a function of the transmitted angle, polarization,
wavelength, and the material’s intrinsic optical properties. A transmissive material may transmit
electromagnetic radiation in one of the following two ways. First, as a collimated beam of light
propagates through the material it may be scattered into a hemisphere of 2 p steradians upon exiting
the material. Materials that exhibit this type of property (Scattered Transmittance, Ts) are called
translucent.

Secondly, if the transmitted beam is parallel to the incident beam across the width of the entire
beam, the transmittance is referred to as Collimated Transmittance (Tc). Materials of this type are
called transparent.

Utilizing either the Cary 5000 UV/VIS/NIR reflectometer, the SOC-100 or SOC-400T IR reflectometer
HDR or T measurements can be made from the UV out to the very long IR. Data is recorded directly to
ASCII text files on the PC and is importable into Excel or other spreadsheet software.

# ASTM Testing

## Specializing in a variety of ASTM compliant testing

ASTM standards for optical property testing are developed through a collaborative process involving
industry and scientific experts. This ensures that the testing procedures are accurate and
repeatable for material analysis. Surface Optics has actively contributed to defining these testing
methodologies, leveraging decades of experience as an optical property testing lab and
instrumentation manufacturer. Our lab is fully equipped to assist research, construction, and
manufacturing clients by providing measurement services that adhere to the relevant ASTM standards.

# Solar Reflectance (SRI/TSR)

## Fast, Accurate Solar Reflectance, TSR, and SRI testing

Solar reflectance is the measure of a material’s ability to reflect solar energy from its surface.
It is expressed as a percentage or a value between 0 and 1, where 0 indicates no reflectance
(complete absorption of solar energy) and 1 indicates total reflectance (no absorption of solar
energy). With our decades of experience and commitment to quality, you can trust our lab to deliver
accurate, solar reflectance data that moves your project forward.

GET A QUOTE

## 410 Series Measurements

The 410 Series can produce the following measured values:

Building material energy efficiency
CSP performance optimization
Urban heat island effect studies
Automotive heat transfer
Solar Reflectance Index
Spacecraft thermal management

Does your lab’s measurement of solar reflectance, thermal emittance, and SRI comply with LEED
requirements?

Our lab measures solar reflectance according to ASTM C1549, thermal emittance according to ASTM E408
and calculate SRI according to ASTM E-1980. LEED has multiple versions and the program undergoes
changes so we recommend you confirm with your project reviewer at USGBC that using a lab that
measures SRI inputs according to those ASTMs is acceptable before moving forward with our services.

Do you provide solar reflectance (SR) measurements for hardscape / paving materials?

Yes! Our lab is experienced in handling these types of materials and can provide a solar reflectance
testing report. Many green building programs only require solar reflectance measurements and not a
full SRI report for hardscape materials.

# Solar Absorptance & Thermal Emittance Measurements

## Precise solar absorptance measurements for thermal control

Utilizing cutting-edge solar reflectometers, our lab provides precise measurements of a material’s
ability to absorb solar radiation. Our comprehensive testing solutions help optimize photovoltaic
panels, solar thermal collectors, and energy-efficient building materials. With our decades of
experience and commitment to quality, you can trust us to deliver accurate, reliable data that
enhances your solar energy projects.

[GET A QUOTE][64]

## Applications

Solar panel efficiency
Building energy performance
Thermal insulation testing
Spacecraft thermal control
Solar water heater design
Photovoltaic materials
Architectural material selection
Automotive heat transfer
Solar energy harvesting

## What is solar absorptance?

Solar absorptance (α) is the fraction of the incident solar energy that is absorbed by a material.
It ranges from 0 to 1, where 0 indicates that no solar energy is absorbed (all is reflected or
transmitted), and 1 indicates that all solar energy is absorbed (none is reflected or transmitted).

## Our testing procedures

Surface Optics offers solar absorptance testing in accordance with ASTM E903 and ASTM C1549.

# Optical Properties Measurements Database

The Optical Properties Measurements Database is a centralized resource for accurate, measurements of
material optical characteristics, including solar reflectance, thermal emittance, transmittance,
hemispherical directional reflectance, and BRDF/BTDF.

Developed to support engineers, scientists, and designers working in high-performance
applications—from aerospace and defense to energy and materials science—this database provides
standardized, high-quality data collected using calibrated instrumentation in controlled laboratory
settings.

### [Silicon Carbide][64]

Silicon carbide (SiC) is a super-hard, high-performance material known for its excellent thermal,
mechanical, and electrical properties. It’s especially valuable in extreme environments where other
materials would fail.

# Vacuum Deposition Coatings

## Surface Optics is a focused provider of vacuum deposition coatings for the aerospace and defense
## industries. We have over 30 years of space hardware coating experience.

Our coatings lab offers large chambers and clean rooms, a custom job environment, one-of-a-kind
coating hardware, significant space program heritage, and on-site world-class metrology. We
manufacture vacuum deposited coatings using several techniques standard in the coating industry:
resistively heated thermal evaporation, electron beam evaporation, and ion beam assisted deposition.

Utilize our standard coating services or work with us to develop a custom solution that meets your
needs. We perform batch-to-batch adjustment and verification with our [in-house measurement
lab][64]. Our ability to scale, test, and measure within the same facility allows us to rapidly
bring your development project from prototype to production. Capability to scale for high volume
production and large substrates.

# Low Observable / Stealth Coatings

## Spectrally tailored pigments are incorporated into paint or ink formulations with application and
## cure mechanics specifically tailored to customer end-use

We use optical coating expertise to create unique, spectrally tailored paints. Releasable PVD thin
film coatings are processed into spectrally tailored flake pigment. Wavelength-dependent reflectance
and absorption can be customized to customer requirements using design principles of optical
interference coatings.

## Innovative Roll-to-Roll Process

Our unique roll-to-roll coating process was developed in-house for Electron Beam, Jori Source, and
Ion-assisted deposition (IAD) of metallic and dielectric films (all processes scalable).

1.8m and 5m chambers accommodate a variety of applications, with deposition on film up to 1000m x
1.5m wide and a great deal of experience handling sub-10 μm films.

### **Developed by SOC**

A unique capability of our lab

### **Substrate moves across 4 banks of e-beam guns**

Allowing up to 4 discrete layers per pass.

### **PID programmed rate monitoring**

Allows for precise uniform thickness deposition.

### **Film conversion Re-Winder**

Cleanroom film handling (ISO Class 5), at atmosphere for pre and post processing.

## Modeling

Surface Optics maintains a variety of analytical models to predict surface scattering and heat
transfer. The test data for each surface design will provide inputs to these models to provide an
iteration to the development process.

### ****In-house developed Scattering Coatings Computer-Aided Design (ScatCad) program****

Predicts spectral BRDF and HDR of coatings and surfaces. First principles radiative transfer model,
includes binder absorption. Based on optical constants and micro-physical composition. Provides
analysis of diffusely scattering surfaces.

### ****Surface Optics developed ENSemble of InfraRed (ENSIR) analysis code****

Used to predict the performance of the spectrally tailored coating. Optical coatings mapped to
surface elements. User defined multispectral environment. Coupled finite element radiance and
internal/external thermodynamic heat flows. Embedded MODTRAN atmospherics.

# Large Area Coatings

SOC uses an electron beam (Ebeam) evaporation, physical vapor deposition (PVD) process to coat large
area coatings up to 2.5-3m in diameter (depending on geometry) in a batch system, or 60” wide in our
Roll to Roll system.

All batch and roll to roll processes can be scaled up from a development system capable of coating
up to 3 development trials per day. The ability to scale, test, and measure within the same facility
allows us to bring your development project from prototype to production rapidly.

We can perform batch-to-batch adjustment and verification with an in-house measurement lab.

All work is performed in an ISO9001 clean room environment. AS9100 certified facility.

Scalability: Excellent

### 5m & 3m Chamber Key Coating Technologies
* **Multisource ebeam evaporation: **Reflective & Transmissive Coatings, optical, IR, RF
* **High volume crystal rate monitoring: **Automatic changing with dual head with up to 48 crystals
per source for continuous processing
* **Multihead Ion Assisted Deposition: **Index control, durability
* **Jori Source Deposition for dielectric layers: **Mechanical protection, stress and emissivity
management
* **Reflective Coatings: **Tailored thermal control properties
* **Low Temperature coating of flexible polymer substrates**

# Roll-to-Roll Coatings

Our unique roll-to-roll coating process was developed in-house for Electron Beam, Jori Source and
Ion Assisted Deposition (IAD) of metallic and dielectric films (all processes scalable).

1.8m and 5m chambers accommodate a variety of applications, with deposition on film up to 1000m x
1.5m wide and a great deal of experience handling sub-10 µm films.

Substrates move across four banks of e-beam guns, allowing up to four discrete layers per pass, and
PID programmed rate monitoring allows for precise thickness deposition.

Capability to process roll to roll film in a Rewinder cleanroom room (ISO class 5).

# Diamond-Like Carbon Coating

## Improve Durability with Diamond-Like Carbon

Diamond-like carbon (DLC) coatings have a broad range of industrial applications due to their
superior mechanical properties such as high hardness, low friction, and promising wear resistance.
Our DLC coatings are low absorption protective coating with little shift. Deposited using a Filtered
Cathodic Arc Instrument.

### Performance
* Capability only available in large chamber.
* 3m Flat up to 2.5 meter in diameter using translating stage.
* 3m up to 24” without additional tooling using a planetary.

### Mil-Spec
* Eraser rub test per Mil-C-4849A 3.4.3.1 and adhesion per 3.4.1.1. Minimal infrared absorption.

# Vacuum Deposited Gold (VDG) Coatings

Vacuum-deposited gold coatings provide an ultra-thin, highly reflective, and durable layer ideal for
a range of applications, from optical instrumentation to space technology. This precision coating
method ensures consistent coverage and high purity, making it perfect for surfaces that require
reliable thermal and electrical conductivity, as well as corrosion resistance. Vacuum deposition
also enables superior adhesion and customization, allowing the coating to withstand challenging
environments while delivering exceptional optical and thermal properties.

Our VDG coating processes have been certified by major aerospace corporations such as Northrup
Grumman, Lockheed Martin, JPL, and Raytheon. Coatings can be modified to enhance reflection,
durability, and wavelength range.

# Anti-Reflection (AR) Coatings

SOC offers a standard visible anti-reflection (AR) coating on your substrate. Theoretical design
below assume substrate is glass, near normal angle of incidence, and both sides are coated. Our
in-house design and measurement capabilities allow us to customize this coating to your substrate
and application.

### Performance

** %R 400-700nm Average:** 0.66%

**Thickness Uniformity: **+/- 5% for flat surfaces.

**Turnaround time:** Flat Substrates up to 5” – 2-3 weeks

**Larger than 5 inches: **Development program built with your statement of work.

**Scalability:** Requires Development to scale

### Sample Program

SOC coated the visible anti reflection coating for the primary window for the National Ignition
facility. The large area 3m chamber was used with a single point rotation and a translating source.
The 1 meter window was coated on both sides.

### Sample Program

**THERMAL COVERS FOR NUSTAR OPTICS MODULES**

The Nuclear Spectroscopy Telescope Array (NuSTAR) optics modules required a cover that provided
acceptable thermal and physical properties while maintaining transparency throughout the NuSTAR
band. The front surface of the cover, which points toward space, is coated with 0.08μm of Al then
1.2 μm of SiOX. The back surface, which faces the optics module, is coated with 0.08μm of Al. The
combination of carrier film and coating is >97% transmissive at 6 keV for a single layer.

# Spaceflight and Thermal Control Coatings

Over 30 years of experience in the design, development, and application of precision thermal control
and reflectance coatings on critical spaceflight hardware.

Surface Optics has full capability to address unique hardware from conception to completion. Our
ability to create specialized fixturing includes mechanical design, fabrication, proof loading, and
complete handling plans. Surface Optics has safely processed hundreds of flight reflectors and other
aerospace hardware through our coating facility.

## Key Coating Technology

### Ion Assisted E-beam Evaporation

Reflective & Transmissive coatings: optical, IR, RF.

### Moving Source Coating Platform

Enables coating of parts as large as chamber.

### Low temperature coating of polymer substrates

Plastic lens, nano-laminate structures.

### Aluminum coating with tailored thermal control properties

RF coating for composite spaceflight reflectors.

## Your Trusted Partner Across Decades of Space Missions

Chandra
Launched 1999 WMAP
Launched 2001 Kepler Space Telescope
Launched 2009 AEHF
Launched 2010 NuSTAR
Launched 2012 Jason-3
Launched 2016 InSIGHT
Launched 2018 Sentinel-6
Launched 2020 SWOT
Launched 2022 Nancy Grace Roman
Estimated Launch: 2025

## Thermal Control Coating Process

### Composite substrate preparation

Epoxy resin wash coat, thermally condition, Gritblast, Matte finish (BR127 typical).

### Measure resin surface prior to coating

Measure specularity on reflector surface using SOC handheld spectrometer. Measure DC resistivity to
ensure electrical isolation.

### Vapor deposition aluminum (VDA)

Low solar absorptivity (α), in correct thickness for lowest op. frequency.

### Overcoat (SiOX or SiO2)

Correct thickness to yield desired value of emissivity (ε).

### Measure RF Conductivity, α, ε, and Specularity

Using witness / edge coupons, and directly on critical hardware using handheld reflectometer.

**HIGH REFLECTANCE COATING FOR KEPLER PRIMARY MIRROR
**In order to produce a space telescope system with sufficient sensitivity to detect relatively
small planets, a very high reflectance coating on the primary mirror was required. Using ion
assisted evaporation, Surface Optics Corp. applied a protective nine-layer silver coating to enhance
reflection and a dielectric interference coating to minimize the formation of color centers and
atmospheric moisture absorption.

relevant_companies.polished_summary: Surface Optics Corporation specializes in advanced imaging systems, scientific instruments, and thin film vacuum coatings for surface engineering, focusing on the application, characterization, and control of optical properties of surfaces. With a robust portfolio that includes lab and portable reflectometers, emissometers, and hyperspectral cameras, the company serves diverse markets such as aerospace, defense, solar energy, and materials science, providing innovative solutions for research and quality control. Trusted for over 50 years, Surface Optics Corporation is dedicated to delivering precise and reliable measurement tools to meet the evolving needs of its customers.
relevant_companies.audit_reasoning: The company manufactures hyperspectral imaging products that align with the specified market scope, confirming their operation within the spectral sensor market.

_presentation_enrich.specialty_focus: Advanced imaging systems, scientific instruments, and thin film vacuum coatings for surface engineering

relevant_companies.company_summary: Telops is a global leader in amplification, detection, and imaging technologies, specializing in innovative solutions for various applications, including defense, life sciences, industrial control, and nuclear sectors. The company offers a diverse range of products, such as cameras, detectors, image intensifier tubes, and measurement systems, designed to enhance safety and operational efficiency across its target markets.

# Telops

## Hyperspectral and Infrared Innovation

Photonis, Xenics and El-Mul are now unified under the Exosens brand. [Read more →][116]
1. [ Home ][117]
2. [ All brands ][118]
3. Telops

[Copy] [Mail] [Whatsapp] [LinkedIn]

Telops, now known as Exosens, is a renowned brand in hyperspectral imaging systems and infrared
cameras, located in Quebec City, Canada. Telops/Exosens specializes in the design and manufacture of
high-performance systems for defense, industrial, and academic research applications. Additionally,
it offers R&D services in optical systems development, tailored to meet the specific needs of its
customers. If you require state-of-the-art thermal imaging solutions, our company offers the right
technologies to meet your exacting standards.

Since its establishment in 2000, Telops, now operating under Exosens, has built a reputation for
excellence in personnel quality and an innovative approach to the challenges of the optics and
photonics field. Today, the expertise of Telops’ (Exosens) scientists, engineers, and technicians,
and the exceptional performance of its infrared cameras and hyperspectral imagers, are recognized
internationally. Whether you are seeking equipment, expertise, or subcontracting for your optical
systems projects, Telops/Exosens is dedicated to surpassing your high expectations and transforming
them into successful outcomes.

Telops’ global presence is strengthened by an efficient worldwide network of distribution and
representative agents. The company understands the significance of accessibility and customer
support, aiming to provide seamless experiences for clients regardless of their location.

Passion drives Telops, now known as Exosens, and it takes pride in exceeding expectations. Customers
trust Telops/Exosens for its technical expertise, exceptional product quality, and unwavering
commitment to customer satisfaction. By choosing us, customers select a partner dedicated to their
success.

Read more
[Telops]

Telops designs and manufactures high-performance hyperspectral imaging systems and infrared cameras
for defense, industrial, and academic research applications.

### Our products

From SWIR to LWIR, Telops (Exosens) product portfolio includes advanced infrared imaging
technologies designed for a wide range of demanding applications.   The company also provides
state-of-the-art hyperspectral imaging solutions that combine spatial and spectral analysis to
identify materials, detect gases, and characterize scenes based on their unique spectral signatures.

Explore our product lines below to discover how our technologies can support your needs.

Its core offerings include advanced hyperspectral imagery, free open data for research and validation, and a growing archive library of historical imagery, catering to industries such as agriculture, energy, mining, and forestry. By leveraging cutting-edge satellite technology, Wyvern aims to enhance accessibility to critical data for a better understanding of our planet.

Our Mission

# Better access.
# A better earth.

High-resolution hyperspectral imagery gives organizations the clarity they need to make smarter,
more sustainable decisions—and the power to approach pressing environmental problems in completely
new ways.

We’re creating a better Earth by making exceptional hyperspectral data widely accessible and easy to
use.

Our story

## A sustainable future for all

Our founders believed deeply in the potential of hyperspectral imagery to drive positive change.

Since launching our first satellites in 2023, we’re proving what’s possible: better wildfire
mitigation, higher crop yields with fewer pesticides, faster wellsite reclamation, and other
advances that serve the planet.

With more than ten times the precision and detail of other remote sensors, our high-resolution
hyperspectral sensors reveal critical hidden information about the planet, monitor environmental
changes in near-real time, and transform the way organizations respond.

That’s why we’re focused on making the highest-quality data available to as many people as possible.
When we increase access to this powerful tool, we empower widespread stewardship of our home.

Our impact

## Expanding our view

Wyvern’s hyperspectral imaging identifies materials and detect subtle environmental shifts with
incredible accuracy.

Our growing, 5-satellite constellation delivers a steady stream of insight-rich data

4.9M

We’ve imaged 4.9M square kilometres of Earth, and counting, through global tasking

100+

The number of free hyperspectral images in our Open Data program increases each month

## Join us on our mission

Our team is re-inventing the satellite to deliver the highest-resolution hyperspectral data in the
solar system. We seek creative, dedicated individuals to help us build a sustainable future for
humanity.

## Our constellation is growing fast

We’re a rapidly growing hyperspectral imaging company in Western Canada, powered by humans who are
passionate about space and committed to excellence. If you’re excited about increasing the
capability of space-based cameras, creating products that will revolutionize model-based
predictions, or just collaborating to build amazing things—we want you on our team.

## Mission perks

Joining our crew has its benefits:

Unlimited vacation (seriously)

An employee stock option plan

Stellar health and dental benefits (including fertility coverage, 100% prescription coverage, and
lots more)

All the best aspects of startup culture, like whole-team support when and where you need it

Ample opportunities for professional development

A strong sense of ownership over your work

On-sites with team-building activities

Flexible working hours

Hybrid work opportunities

Working on space stuff!

Our values

## How we work

Our team is caring and supportive. We learn, grow, and progress together—personally and
professionally.

### We think outside the cube[sat]

We drive innovation by thinking beyond what’s expected or even currently possible

### We’re committed to a better future

Our technology serves a broader goal: a sustainable future for everyone

### We communicate openly and honestly

We succeed when we’re true to ourselves and our collective mission

### We are reflective, receptive & responsive

We thoughtfully examine our actions, welcome feedback, and embrace change

### We encourage originality

We foster a workplace where everyone’s comfortable bringing their whole self

### We take initiative and persevere

We have a bias to action and approach problems with tenacity and resilience

Diversity, equity, and inclusion

## everyone is
## welcome here

Starting with our gender-diverse leadership team, Wyvern is built on belonging, mutual respect, and
kindness.

We share the responsibility of ensuring everyone feels heard and valued—and we believe that
welcoming employees of all backgrounds, experiences, and lifestyles only expands what’s possible.

When we empower our true selves and embrace our uniqueness, we rise together.

If you require accommodations to participate in our hiring process, please reach out at
[hiring@wyvern.space][24].

## Join us on our mission

Our team is re-inventing the satellite to deliver the highest-resolution hyperspectral data in the
solar system. We seek creative, dedicated individuals to help us build a sustainable future for
humanity.

## Our constellation is growing fast

We’re a rapidly growing hyperspectral imaging company in Western Canada, powered by humans who are
passionate about space and committed to excellence. If you’re excited about increasing the
capability of space-based cameras, creating products that will revolutionize model-based
predictions, or just collaborating to build amazing things—we want you on our team.

## Mission perks

Joining our crew has its benefits:

Unlimited vacation (seriously)

An employee stock option plan

Stellar health and dental benefits (including fertility coverage, 100% prescription coverage, and
lots more)

All the best aspects of startup culture, like whole-team support when and where you need it

Ample opportunities for professional development

A strong sense of ownership over your work

On-sites with team-building activities

Flexible working hours

Hybrid work opportunities

Working on space stuff!

Our values

## How we work

Our team is caring and supportive. We learn, grow, and progress together—personally and
professionally.

### We think outside the cube[sat]

We drive innovation by thinking beyond what’s expected or even currently possible

### We’re committed to a better future

Our technology serves a broader goal: a sustainable future for everyone

### We communicate openly and honestly

We succeed when we’re true to ourselves and our collective mission

### We are reflective, receptive & responsive

We thoughtfully examine our actions, welcome feedback, and embrace change

### We encourage originality

We foster a workplace where everyone’s comfortable bringing their whole self

### We take initiative and persevere

We have a bias to action and approach problems with tenacity and resilience

Diversity, equity, and inclusion

## everyone is
## welcome here

Starting with our gender-diverse leadership team, Wyvern is built on belonging, mutual respect, and
kindness.

We share the responsibility of ensuring everyone feels heard and valued—and we believe that
welcoming employees of all backgrounds, experiences, and lifestyles only expands what’s possible.

When we empower our true selves and embrace our uniqueness, we rise together.

# See the full spectrum

Hyperspectral imagery reveals the chemical and physical properties of the Earth’s surface in
unprecedented detail.

[Order imagery][24][
Contact us
][25]

## Insights in
## every pixel

Hyperspectral sensors capture material-level information and subtle environmental changes that other
sensors miss. Our exceptional imagery offers a true view of ground conditions and greater confidence
operating in complex, fast-changing environments.

We offer multiple ways to access our high-resolution hyperspectral imagery:

## Flexible access to our images

We’re on a mission to make high-quality hyperspectral imagery widely accessible. We offer multiple
ways to get started from on-demand imaging to free, open data.

### Satellite tasking

On-demand hyperspectral imaging tailored to specific times, locations, and spectral requirements.
Choose from standard and premium tasking for new imagery collection.

### Assured capacity

Pre-reserved imaging capacity for high-priority and emergency areas of interest. Guarantee
consistent, uninterrupted collection during competitive imaging seasons.

### The archive library

A growing collection of historical hyperspectral imagery for testing, trend analysis, and model
training. Our archive contains global imagery from 2023 onwards.

### Open data

Free, unrestricted access to 100+ high-resolution images from our constellation. Test and validate
new applications, accelerate product development, and explore the potential of hyperspectral
imagery.

Multispectral imagery only captures a few broad spectral bands—not enough to see the underlying
chemistry of a target. Hyperspectral imagery shows you what matters.

contrasted against surrounding unburned vegetation. Taken with Dragonette-001 on 2024-08-08 at
17:14:53 UTC.

the mining complex and surrounding terrain. Taken with Dragonette-004 on 2025-09-02 at 01:43:55 UTC.
